content: The Harvard Atherosclerosis Reversibility Project (HARP) was designed to investigate the effects of intensive lipid-lowering therapy in patients with normal cholesterol levels (normocholesterolemic patients). The primary focus was to evaluate whether this therapy could influence the progression of atherosclerosis as assessed by coronary angiography over a five-year period. Repeat coronary angiograms were conducted to monitor changes in the progression of coronary atherosclerosis. The study demonstrated significant improvements in total cholesterol, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) levels in patients undergoing intensive lipid-lowering therapy. However, the repeat coronary angiograms did not reveal any significant differences in the degree of coronary obstruction, the progression of coronary stenosis, regression of atherosclerotic lesions, or the incidence of clinical cardiac events. In conclusion, the findings of this study indicate that intensive lipid-lowering therapy does not alter the rate of progression of coronary stenosis in patients with normal cholesterol levels.
